claims.subject: film cooling in regeneratively cooled chambers
claims.object: all of the major regeneratively cooled chambers (Table VIII), usually from the injector
claims.statement: In all of the major regeneratively cooled chambers supplemental cooling is derived from film cooling, normally provided from the injector, to reduce wall thermal severity, give a more acceptable chemical environment, or both.
claims.quote: in all of the major regeneratively cooled chambers supplemental

claims.subject: film-coolant quantity prediction
claims.object: accurate a priori prediction methods; predictions are rough estimates, so designs should keep flexibility
claims.statement: Accurate film-cooling prediction methods are not available; the major unknown is the interaction of the film with the combustion gases, so predictions are rough estimates rather than absolute requirements and the design should allow for later changes.
claims.quote: accurate prediction methods still are not available

claims.subject: film-coolant injection hardware
claims.object: a ring of orifices around the injector periphery, parallel to or against the wall, constant orifice diameter and spacing; selective sizing at hot streaks
claims.statement: Film coolant is normally injected through a ring of orifices around the injector periphery, directed parallel to or against the wall, usually with constant orifice diameter and spacing; selective orifice sizing (larger at hot streaks) gives circumferentially uniform wall temperatures, and wall-impinging and non-impinging streams are combined.
claims.quote: normally injected through a ring of orifices around the periphery of the injector

claims.subject: convergent-section film injection through short tubes
claims.object: an accepted supplemental-cooling technique (manifolding, structural integrity and assembly unresolved)
claims.statement: Film-coolant injection in the convergent section via short tubes between coolant tubes achieved only limited success and is not an accepted technique; barrier cooling (low-O/F elements next to the wall) is an alternative or supplement.
claims.quote: Currently, this method is not an accepted technique for supplemental cooling
